content:
Just one month after raising trade-in values for most of its products, Apple has updated those amounts once again — this time after its "Surprise and Shine" event wraps up. iPhone trade-in prices have been lowered, while iPad and most Mac models have seen increases. Here's a look at the latest values.

Apple is now accepting the iPhone Air and the iPhone 17 lineup as trade-ins

Last month, Apple updated the trade-in price list for its iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch models, Mac lineup, and Android devices, with some devices seeing increases of nearly 30%.

Apple has now updated trade-in values once again — every iPhone model accepted for trade-in has had its maximum credit reduced, with some models dropping by as much as $120.

Meanwhile, the entire iPad lineup and every Mac except the Mac Pro have had their trade-in values raised; Apple Watch and Android device trade-in values are mostly lower or unchanged.
